ai.description: *Oligodon dorsalis* is a small, slender snake reaching 30–40 cm. It is greyish-brown with a distinct dark V-shaped neck mark and a prominent black spot on the tail. It belongs to the family Colubridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Oligodon dorsalis* is best identified by the distinct, dark V-shaped marking on the nape and a prominent black spot on the dorsal surface of the tail.
ai.habitat: *Oligodon dorsalis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found in leaf litter and undergrowth at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,500m.
ai.behavior: The Spot-tailed Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into reptile eggs, its primary food source.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon dorsalis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon dorsalis* is found in Northeast India (Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting elevations up to 1,500 meters.
